doc.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019

title: Upcoming plans, albums and closing
summary: He is heading to Eastman, then home to teach, and is weighing a chamber or tango album or a septet album; Rowe closes the interview.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: No, no. What’s the very next thing on your plate?
I have to go to Rochester.

Yeah, I’m going to Eastman and then after that I go back home and start teaching. And then I’m getting together thoughts for another album. I’m planning — I don’t know which way I should go. I have all this chamber music I want to do and Argentinean — I do a lot of tangos. So I’m starting to work with these people now in New York and development of those connections and I don’t know if I want to do a chamber music album, different than it was with Argentinean influence. By the way the last album was recorded in Buenos Aires and then I came back and added some of the American guys you know. But the basic tracks were done down there and we toured it and it was really fun. So between that and doing an album with four horns and just a regular straight ahead jazz septet kind of album so we’re deciding which one and looking for funding, how to make this happen. I feel pretty fortunate to be able to keep doing this. That’s what I can say, yeah.
Well that’s a good note to wrap up on. Thank you very much.
My great pleasure. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
